cells.tense: Here, now, with the pen still in your hand, you keep something you're building alive and warm for whoever comes near it.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Before you settle the next stretch of what you're making, tell whoever's in it with you about a part you still can't picture — the open one, not the plan — and leave that patch uncovered where they can see it too.
cells.core:
You keep what you're building warm without needing to hold every piece of it. Steady hands, real heat — that's what a good keeper looks like. And a fire doesn't need the same hand at every hour; it needs the person who started it to trust the next hour to someone else.

So the work is narrower than holding on: on a piece that isn't settled yet, show them the patch whose shape you can't make out — not the tidy version, the open one — and stay with it while they look at it too. What you get: a decision you didn't have to carry alone. What you get: the fire is theirs to keep as well.
cells.sheetLine: You can share the warmth, not just the flame.
cells.verb: Tending the fire for what you're building
cells.place: Beside the person being met, where what you're making stays lit

cells.tense: You're bracing at a future that can't be written in yet, settling how the shared thing will go before anyone inside it gets a say.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Before the next hard thing about what you share gets said, check who's there to hear it. Say it at the size they can take in now, and sit with holding the rest back.
cells.core:
You've been protecting what you share by holding every future version of it in your own hands. From where you stand that's strength. From the other side, the grip reads as a hand closed around something the others thought they'd get to shape. They've gone quiet about the parts they'd like to keep.

What's thin here isn't care. It's the honesty that lets a person stand next to you on ground that isn't settled yet. Say the hard thing gently, once, at the size that can be heard right now — the piece that fits, not the whole truth — and give the other person room to answer that piece.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided the future before anyone asked how it feels.
cells.verb: Tending the fire for what you're building
cells.place: Beside the person being met, where what you're making stays lit

cells.tense: You're still at a door that's already behind you, waiting to be called back to something you used to keep lit.
cells.act: provide for the growth by knowing what to let go
cells.ask: Clear out whatever the old shared thing no longer needs — a habit, a role, a way you used to show up. Leave where it sat bare, with nothing new moved in yet.
cells.core:
The shared thing finished a while back and your week still schedules it. The same words get said at the same hour, the same slot sits reserved, and hours that could go to something alive wait on a day you're holding open for someone who no longer comes. The light stays on for a room nobody's in.

Put one wanted thing where the finished one sits — work, a walk, something fresh you've meant to try. Go there in the old hour, and let the finished way end by giving way to something else. What you get: the hours the dead thing was holding, handed back to you. Nobody needs telling it's over — the hour holds something else now.
cells.sheetLine: It ended. You've gone on keeping the light on.
cells.verb: Tending the fire for what you're building
cells.place: Beside the person being met, where what you're making stays lit

cells.tense: Here in an unwitnessed present, pen down in a room where the writing is already happening, you keep something alive for people who never see whose hand is on it.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: This week, rework the shape held by the people you gather with, by one real inch — a rule, a way you meet — and do it yourself before anyone asks. Small, but signed.
cells.core:
Something in what you share is already shifting — how you gather, the tale that gets passed around about the group — and it's moving because you quietly stopped renewing the old shape. Ask and the answer comes back that you didn't notice. The shift is getting made, and nobody, including you, is signing for it.

Give it one real inch this week. Not a speech, not the whole rebuild — one small turn in how the shared thing works, done by your hand, with someone watching you do it. What you get: a change with a date on it instead of a thinning only the others can feel. When someone asks, there's a hand to point at.
cells.sheetLine: Something shared is shifting. Your hand is on it.
